title: Behaviour and Design of Steel Structures
description: Behaviour and design of trusses, frames, members and connections in steel building and bridge structures. Ultimate strength, stability, and postbuckling are emphasized in topical examples including: plate girders; composite steel/concrete girders; second-order frame behaviour; high-strength bolted and welded framing connections. Other topics include: concrete filling; fire protection and plastic analysis of hollow structural section connections. Canadian Design Standards and the Limit States Design concepts are used.
notes: Credit will be granted for only one of CIVE 557, CIVE 457.
May be offered as a joint undergraduate and graduate class.
